back: A group of organisms of one species, living in the same area, at the same time.
All of the populations of different species in an ecosystem.
A unit containing the community of organisms and their environment, interacting together.
notes: Examples: a lake, a vlei, a rotting log.

front: Factors that affect the rate of population growth?
back: Food supply, competition, predation and disease.

front: The four phases of a sigmoid growth curve?
Why is growth slow in the lag phase?
back: Few individuals; they are adjusting to new conditions (e.g. making enzymes) before reproducing quickly.

front: Why is growth rapid in the exponential phase?
back: Plenty of food and space, little competition, few wastes: birth rate much greater than death rate.

front: What happens in the stationary phase?
back: Limiting factors (food shortage, toxic waste, competition) make the birth rate equal the death rate.
The largest population of a species that an environment can support over a long period.
notes: Set by limiting factors: water, food, oxygen, space, shelter.

back: Habitat degradation, overgrazing, soil erosion, disease and starvation.
notes: Example: elephants crowding at Hwange waterholes in the dry season.
